newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty steady, eyes U.S. vote and dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty steady, eyes U.S. vote and dlr/mark.

text.p: Polish zloty finished the slow Monday session a fraction stronger against the basket of currencies but all eyes were on dollar/mark swings ahead of U.S. presidential elections on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said foreign investors, which have often moved the shallow domestic market that is basically neutral when left on its own, would likely hold off from large-scale manouvers ahead of the election outcome or more news about Russian president Boris Yetlsin's upcoming heart operation.
"Not much is happening here before the U.S. poll and Yeltsin's bypass," said Maciej Graborz of Bank Zachodni SA.
The zloty closed at 1.95/1.92 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Thursday's close at 1.88/1.83 percent.
It was at 2.8125/30 to the dollar, flat from last week's 2.8120/35 and at 1.8575/85 per mark, up from 1.8580/90.
Dealers said markets have already counted in a U.S. presidential win of incumbent Bill Clinton, which would likely keep the dollar in its band between 1.51 and 1.53 marks.

At today's 1.2 billion-zloty primary T-bill auction minimum prices of all bills fell 0.01 point as investors placed bids for 899 million zlotys and the ministry sold 611 million zlotys worth of bills.
The average yield of the benchmark 52-week paper rose 0.03 point to 19.50 percent, while the 26-week yield increased 0.02 to 19.18. The 13-week T-bill yield held flat at 18.55 percent.
On the money market one-day rates inched up as banks wanted to build up required reserve levels at the start of the month.
Overnight rates closed at 19.95/20.25 percent, just up from opening's 19.80/20.20 and tomorrow/next at 19.95/20.25 percent, flat from this morning's 19.90/20.40 percent.
